title: HGMA Run 2026 Review: Surabaya's Medical-Association Half Marathon at Stadion Brawijaya
seo_title: HGMA Run 2026 Review: Course, Tips & Registration Guide
meta_description: HGMA Run 2026 review: October 11 at Stadion Brawijaya, Surabaya. 21K, 10K, and 5K organised by IHGMA. Race conditions, registration via Amasol, and what East Java runners need to know.
dek: The HGMA Run 2026 brings the Indonesian Healthy Gymnastics Medical Association (IHGMA) into the Surabaya road-racing calendar, anchoring a three-distance event at Stadion Brawijaya on October 11, 2026. With 21.1K, 10K, and 5K options, a central-city stadium venue, and registration channelled through the Amasol platform, this is a community-health-flavoured race in Indonesia's second-largest city — and one that Surabaya's growing running community will want to track.
verdict: The HGMA Run occupies an interesting niche in the Indonesian running landscape: it is a race organised by a medical association (IHGMA — the Indonesian Healthy Gymnastics Medical Association), which means the event carries an implicit health-promotion mandate that most commercial road races do not. The venue, Stadion Brawijaya, is a central-city sports complex in Surabaya with good transport links and proper facilities — a significant step up from the roadside-start races that still characterise much of the Indonesian provincial circuit. Three distances (21.1K, 10K, 5K) cover the full participation spectrum, and the October 11 date falls at the tail end of East Java's dry season, meaning warm but manageable morning conditions. The registration infrastructure is in place — the Amasol platform (rm.amasol.co.id) is listed as the official registration channel, and Amasol has powered numerous Indonesian road races — but registration is not yet open as of this writing, which is consistent with the Indonesian pattern of opening registration two to three months before race day. The unknowns are consistent with a medical-association-organised event: the course map has not been published, on-course medical support (ironically, given the organiser) has not been detailed, and the production values — timing method, aid station frequency, medal and shirt quality — remain unspecified. For Surabaya-based runners, this is a race to put on the radar, particularly given the stadium venue and the three-distance format. For runners elsewhere in Indonesia, wait for the course announcement and registration details before committing to travel.

sections.heading: What Is the HGMA Run?
paragraphs: The HGMA Run is a road race organised by IHGMA — the Indonesian Healthy Gymnastics Medical Association (Ikatan Healthy Gymnastics Medical Association) — scheduled for October 11, 2026, at Stadion Brawijaya in Surabaya, East Java [1]. The event offers three distances: a 21.1K half marathon, a 10K, and a 5K — a format that accommodates serious road racers, recreational runners, and families alike [1].

IHGMA is a medical-professional organisation that promotes health through physical activity, and its involvement as the race organiser gives the HGMA Run a distinctive character: this is a race where the health-promotion mission is baked into the event's DNA, not added as an afterthought through a charity partner [2]. The association's website (ihgma.org) and its presence on Indonesian running calendars suggest an organisation that is serious about building a recurring event rather than a one-off fun run [2].

Registration is listed as being handled through the Amasol platform (rm.amasol.co.id), a registration provider that has powered numerous Indonesian road races [3]. The registration page exists but is not yet accepting sign-ups as of this writing — consistent with the Indonesian pattern of opening registration roughly two to three months before race day [3].

sections.heading: Stadion Brawijaya: Surabaya's Central-City Race Hub
paragraphs: Stadion Brawijaya is a multi-purpose sports complex located in central Surabaya, roughly halfway between the city's commercial core and its southern suburbs [4]. The stadium and its surrounding grounds provide a natural race village: start and finish lines can be set up on the stadium track or in the adjacent parking areas, with the stadium's permanent facilities — toilets, changing rooms, sheltered seating — providing infrastructure that most Indonesian road races (which often start on closed public roads with portable toilets as the only amenities) cannot match [4].

The stadium's central location is well-served by Surabaya's transport network. It is accessible via Jalan Brawijaya and the surrounding road grid, and is within a 15–20 minute drive from most parts of the city [4]. For runners using ride-hailing (Gojek or Grab, both ubiquitous in Surabaya), the stadium is a well-known landmark that drivers will find without difficulty [4].

The area around the stadium is predominantly residential and institutional, with wide roads that can support a road race course with partial or full road closures [4]. The terrain in central Surabaya is flat — Surabaya sits on the coastal plain of eastern Java with no significant elevation changes — meaning the half-marathon course is likely to be fast and accessible, with the only challenge coming from the climate rather than the topography [4].

sections.heading: October 11: End of the Dry Season in East Java
paragraphs: October 11 falls at the very end of East Java's dry season — the transition period before the onset of the northwest monsoon, which typically arrives in November [5]. The weather is characterised by warm mornings (24–27°C), moderate to high humidity (75–85%), and an increasing but still manageable risk of afternoon rain [5].

For a half marathon starting at 5:00–5:30am, runners can expect to finish before 8:00am, when temperatures are still in the mid-to-high 20s. This is warmer than ideal racing conditions but significantly more comfortable than the March–May period, when Surabaya temperatures can exceed 30°C by 8:00am [5]. The humidity will be the primary performance variable — runners should expect to sweat heavily from the opening kilometres and should hydrate at every available aid station [5].

The flat Surabaya terrain partially compensates for the warm conditions. With no hills to break rhythm or spike heart rate, runners can settle into a steady pace and focus on managing their effort through the heat rather than fighting the course itself [4]. For Surabaya-based runners accustomed to training in these conditions year-round, October 11 represents a fair — if not fast — racing day [5].

sections.heading: Registration, the Amasol Platform, and What to Expect
paragraphs: Registration for the HGMA Run 2026 is listed as being handled through the Amasol platform at rm.amasol.co.id [3]. Amasol is a well-established Indonesian event registration provider that handles everything from small community runs to larger regional races — it supports online payment through Indonesian bank transfers and e-wallets, digital bib assignment, and e-certificate delivery [3].

As of this writing, registration is not yet open [3]. Based on the Indonesian race calendar pattern, expect registration to open approximately two to three months before race day (around August–September 2026) [1]. Indonesian half marathon entry fees typically range from IDR 150,000–350,000 for early-bird registration — expect HGMA Run to fall within or slightly below this range, consistent with its community-health orientation [1].

Race-kit inclusions for Indonesian races of this scale typically feature an event shirt (cotton or dry-fit, depending on the organiser's budget), a race bib (likely manual timing rather than chip-based for a community race), and a finisher's medal [1]. The stadium venue means bag-drop facilities are likely to be available in the stadium's permanent infrastructure — a significant convenience over the temporary tent-based bag drops common at roadside-start races [4].

sections.heading: Should You Run the HGMA Run 2026?
paragraphs: If you live in Surabaya or the surrounding East Java region (Sidoarjo, Gresik, Mojokerto, Malang): yes, this race should be on your radar for October 2026. The central stadium venue, the three-distance format, and the flat Surabaya terrain combine to make this a convenient and accessible addition to the East Java running calendar [1][4].

If you are a medical or healthcare professional: the IHGMA connection may add a layer of interest — this is a race organised by your professional community, and the health-promotion framing may come with additional programming (health screenings, medical talks, or wellness exhibitions) that commercial races do not offer [2].

If you are a runner from outside East Java or an international participant: hold off on booking travel until the course map and registration details are published. Surabaya has good air connectivity via Juanda International Airport (SUB) and a range of accommodation from budget to five-star, so the logistics are workable — but the race itself needs to justify the trip, and right now there is not enough published detail to make that case [1][4].
